forecasts.reason: No recipe change: the harness metrics reproduce E010. Whether the 10-seed offset falls within 0.3 pp and the std within 0.15-0.4 pp is likely but uncertain.
With 100 classes, label smoothing 0.3 is probably near-optimal. 0.2 changes accuracy by about −0.1 pp, inside the noise, so the ≥0.3 pp claim is unresolved.
Weights have a fixed norm, so lr sets the angular step size. ×1.5 at momentum 0.6 is probably near flat, and a +0.3 pp gain is unlikely.
Muon takes no weight decay, so only the BN, whitening-bias and head SGD groups are affected. The lever is small, and halving it slightly hurts the head.
The code already uses steps=3, so this is a no-op with bit-identical accuracy.
Steps are GPU-saturated at about 25 ms. Launch overhead is ≤3%, so a ≥3% cut is unlikely, and moving the augmentation may change the RNG stream.
The alpha ramp gives a short EMA horizon, so a plain end-swapped EMA should land within 0.3 pp. The Lookahead pull adds a little at most.

cruxes: How far is the 10-seed (and so the 40-seed) mean of E010 from 0.7548? If it is lower, epochs must be bought back at about 2 s per pp, and every time cut is blocked.
Does any hyperparameter (LS, Muon lr, head wd) give at least +0.3 pp for free? That is the only route to spending margin on time.
What fraction of the 6.6 s is fixed cost (H2D, pad, whitening, first-epoch warm-up) versus per-pixel compute? This decides whether systems work or resizing is the next cut.
structured_output.world_model: The tip is E010: 9.5 epochs, 24/28/32 px resizing, Muon with NS steps=3, Lookahead/EMA, width 512. It runs 6.64 s at 0.7548, a margin of 0.18 pp. Accuracy prices: epochs about 2 s per pp, width about 1.4 s per pp, resizing about 3.5 s per pp. Muon renormalises the weights and takes no weight decay, so the weight-decay lever only reaches the head and biases. NS is already at 3 iterations. Steps are GPU-bound, so launch and graph-break work buys ≤3%. The next win needs a free accuracy gain, then spending it on fewer epochs or 32-px steps.
